title: GST Supply — Taxable Event, Composite Supply and Mixed Supply

content.overview: GST supply covers goods or services for consideration in the course or furtherance of business, plus deemed supplies. A composite supply is naturally bundled and taxed as the principal supply. A mixed supply is two or more independent supplies for one price and is taxed as the supply that attracts the highest rate. Classification changes the rate and the place-of-supply rule. It does not create a supply that section 7 excludes.
content.glance: GST Supply — Taxable Event, Composite Supply and Mixed Supply. Complete Tax treatise with statutory deconstruction, examples, verified authorities, forum analysis and chamber drafting.
content.study: Decide supply first. Then ask whether the items are naturally bundled. If not, and one price covers them, use mixed supply.

cases.facts: The Court examined the components of a valid charging provision.
cases.issue: What must a tax levy clearly identify to be valid?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A valid levy ordinarily identifies the taxable event, person liable, rate and measure or value of the tax.

cases.name: Union of India v. Azadi Bachao Andolan
cases.facts: The Court considered treaty benefits, circulars and tax avoidance arguments.
cases.issue: How should a valid tax treaty and administrative circular operate?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A treaty and valid administrative practice must be respected unless displaced by law; legitimate tax planning is not automatically evasion.
cases.holding: The Court upheld the challenged treaty approach in the circumstances.

cases.name: Union of India v. Mohit Minerals Pvt. Ltd.
cases.facts: The case concerned GST levy and the legal effect of a Council recommendation.
cases.issue: What is the constitutional and statutory force of GST Council recommendations?
cases.ratioDecidendi: GST Council recommendations have persuasive value within the constitutional design but are not automatically binding as primary legislation without statutory implementation.
cases.holding: The Court interpreted the federal GST framework accordingly.
cases.relevance: Use for GST levy, delegated action and constitutional federalism.

enhancement.definition: GST supply covers goods or services for consideration in the course or furtherance of business, plus deemed supplies. A composite supply is naturally bundled and taxed as the principal supply. A mixed supply is two or more independent supplies for one price and is taxed as the supply that attracts the highest rate.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Classification changes the rate and the place-of-supply rule. It does not create a supply that section 7 excludes.
essentialIngredients: Single supply, composite supply or mixed supply
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 8 enacts the classification. Composite supply is supplied together in the ordinary course of business, and the principal supply gives the tax treatment. Mixed supply is not a composite supply, and one price covers independent items. Schedule II classification is separate from this bundling test.
examples: A hotel room sold with breakfast in the ordinary package is tested as a composite supply.
A Diwali hamper of independent goods for one price is tested as a mixed supply.
enhancement.problemApplication: Decide supply first. Then ask whether the items are naturally bundled. If not, and one price covers them, use mixed supply.
